+let idleTimeoutFreeDispatcher: EnvHttpProxyAgent | undefined

+/**
+ * Fetch for providers that may point at a local model server, with undici's
+ * idle timeouts disabled.
+ *
+ * undici aborts a response after `headersTimeout` / `bodyTimeout` (300s
+ * each) of silence on the wire. A local model processing a large prompt
+ * sends its headers at once and then nothing until the first token, often
+ * for longer than that, so the request dies with `UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT`
+ * while the server is still generating (cline/cline#13371, #13464).
+ * Cancellation stays with the request's AbortSignal, i.e. the stop button.
+ *
+ * This goes through undici's own fetch rather than global fetch: the VS Code
+ * extension host wraps global fetch and swaps any caller-supplied dispatcher
+ * for its own default-timeout Agent, so the override would be dropped. The
+ * trade-off is that these requests honour `http_proxy` / `https_proxy` /
+ * `no_proxy` rather than VS Code's `http.proxy` setting. On the standalone
+ * build this is the same proxy agent as the global one above.
+ */
+export const fetchWithoutIdleTimeouts: typeof globalThis.fetch = ((
+	input: string | URL | Request,
+	init?: RequestInit,
+): Promise<Response> => {
+	if (mockFetch) {
+		return mockFetch(input, init)
+	}
+	idleTimeoutFreeDispatcher ??= new EnvHttpProxyAgent({ headersTimeout: 0, bodyTimeout: 0 })

discussion_comments.comment_body: [P1] Preserve the loopback proxy bypass. EnvHttpProxyAgent proxies even localhost/127.0.0.1 when HTTP_PROXY is set and NO_PROXY is absent; VS Code's existing resolver always connects directly to loopback. I reproduced this with the actual exported wrapper: the direct control reached a 127.0.0.1 model server, while fetchWithoutIdleTimeouts sent CONNECT to a rejecting proxy and failed without reaching the model server. This breaks previously working LM Studio/Ollama setups for users launching VS Code with proxy environment variables. Preserve loopback's direct routing and add a regression test with HTTP_PROXY set and NO_PROXY unset (the current tests delete both variables).

discussion_comments.comment_body: Confirmed, undici's `EnvHttpProxyAgent` proxies everything unless `NO_PROXY` matches, same class as the Bun behaviour you fixed in #14401. Fixed: loopback hosts now use a plain no-timeout `Agent` and everything else the env-var proxy agent, mirroring the resolver's always-direct rule. The net test runs with `HTTP_PROXY` set to a recording CONNECT proxy and `NO_PROXY` unset: loopback never reaches it, an unroutable host does. Also verified live in a VS Code extension host launched with `HTTP_PROXY` on a dead port and no `NO_PROXY`: an OpenAI Compatible request to a loopback server completed. Details in the PR description. For the record, the JetBrains build has had this behaviour for all traffic since its global dispatcher is the same agent, so there it was pre-existing rather than a regression.

Same for IPv4-mapped loopback like `[::ffff:127.0.0.1]`, which `isIP` reports as v6 and none of the v6 ranges match. Both would fall back to the regular fetch and keep the 300s timeout. +function isLocalNetworkUrl(baseUrl: string | undefined): boolean {

discussion_comments.comment_body: Known gap, and the trade-off Saoud named in his comment. Resolving DNS at session build would add an async step and a dependency on the resolver's answer at that moment, which is worse than the gap. A user with a LAN server behind a DNS name can use its IP for now. Leaving as is.

Fixed in b7fd827e5b. Command timeouts now use a coalesced, bounded client.list health probe. A successful probe or any other command reply arriving during it keeps the socket and SSH forward alive; only a failed probe with no intervening replies retires the transport. Regression tests cover a slow read with an unrelated pending write, a slow heartbeat while writes receive replies, concurrent timeout probe coalescing, and the real one-way forwarding stall. Writes and prompts are never replayed.

This is now awaited on every session build, so model discovery lands on the task-start path for the first time.

Agent review: 

Only the primary call is bounded, though: when `/api/v1/models` fails, the
fallback `fetchModelIdsFromSource` uses a bare `fetch` with no timeout, so
against a host that drops packets rather than refusing (remote LM Studio, VPN
down) the 5s abort fires and then the fallback hangs — and the task never
starts. Localhost is fine; a closed port fails immediately.

The unbounded fetch is pre-existing, but it previously only stalled webview
surfaces. An AbortSignal in `fetchModelIdsFromSource` would cover it.
